Following an internal strategic review, Bristol Myers Squibb informed Prothena Corporation plc (the “ Company ”) on October 28, 2026 that it has decided not to advance PRX019 further in the clinic. In May 2024, a subsidiary of the Company entered into an exclusive global license agreement for PRX019 with Bristol Myers Squibb (the “ PRX019 Global License Agreement ”) to develop, manufacture and commercialize antibody products globally targeting a specified target (including PRX019, and collectively, “ Licensed Products ”) for any and all uses or purposes with respect to any human or animal disease, disorder or condition, and received an upfront payment of $80 million. The PRX019 License Agreement will terminate on January 28, 2027. In the first half of 2026, the Company completed the Phase 1 trial for PRX019, which successfully demonstrated a benign safety and tolerability profile, no immunogenicity, and dose-dependent pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic effects, meeting the Company’s prespecified pharmacodynamic targets. Pursuant to the PRX019 Global License Agreement, in addition to the upfront payment, the Company was eligible to receive further development, regulatory, and sales milestones of up to $617.5 million. The Company was also eligible to receive tiered royalties on annual, worldwide net sales of Licensed Products. In connection with termination of the PRX019 Global License Agreement, Bristol Myers Squibb will not owe any of the foregoing to the Company. Moponetug and PRX019 are both clinical-stage programs which were part of a research and development collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb executed in 2018. Bristol Myers Squibb continues to develop moponetug (formerly PRX005), a potential best-in-class antibody for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease that specifically targets a key epitope within the microtubule binding region (MTBR) of tau, a protein implicated in the causal pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s disease. Bristol Myers Squibb is conducting the ongoing Phase 2 TargetTau-1 clinical trial in patients with early Alzheimer’s disease (NCT06268886). To date, Bristol Myers Squibb has paid the Company $135 million in licensing payments for moponetug and the Company is eligible to receive up to $562.5 million in regulatory and sales milestones, as well as tiered royalties on annual, worldwide net sales.
